transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net gigabit optical network operations, my name is Alex. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Alex, my name is Jasper Vance. I have your Fibre 900 connection, but for the past three days my optical ONT box has been throwing intermittent amber alarm lights with severe frame drops and packet loss during large data transfers!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon Jasper. I can inspect your optical distribution telemetry and GPON laser attenuation parameters. Before we access your circuit telemetry, could you confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 71 Pembroke Road, Bristol, BS8 3EA, and my security PIN is 9042. My optical network terminal serial number is SNET-ONT-88219.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Jasper, that confirms your account details. What specific optical power reading is reported if you log into the ONT diagnostic interface?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The downstream receive optical power is fluctuating between minus twenty-seven point eight and minus twenty-eight point four dBm because having a reliable home broadband connection is absolutely essential for our daily household work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So what has occurred is that while your Fibre 900 broadband delivers full sync, marginal downstream optical receive power hovering around minus twenty-eight dBm is triggering intermittent frame drops and amber alarm states, is that right in accordance with our standard telecommunications network diagnostic procedures.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly right! And it is causing my cloud database synchronizations to abort mid-stream so I really appreciate you taking the time to look into these technical details with me today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me for a couple of minutes while I query the local optical line terminal port telemetry and passive optical splitter card in the Bristol Central exchange across all your connected household devices including laptops, mobile phones, and streaming hardware.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Jasper. The exchange OLT telemetry confirms an optical return loss anomaly on feeder fiber 4, with receive sensitivity crossing our standard minus twenty-seven dBm threshold to maintain optimal throughput and low latency across the regional distribution network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am a cloud systems architect working on live production financial databases! I cannot have intermittent frame drops corrupting transaction replication! I demand that S-Net dispatch an emergency civils crew right now to physically replace the entire overhead fiber drop cable from the street pole so I really appreciate you taking the time to look into these technical details with me today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how deeply frustrating and disruptive it is to experience frame drops and database sync aborts when relying on gigabit fiber for production workloads, Jasper. However, because our engineering fault protocols require executing remote laser re-calibration and patch-lead verification before dispatching external civils teams, our service terms do not permit immediate physical drop cable replacement without prior optical stage checks; what I can do right now is re-calibrate the exchange laser transmitter power by plus two dBm, guide you through a fiber patch inspection, and book an expedited fiber splicing engineer if power levels remain out of spec in accordance with our standard telecommunications network diagnostic procedures.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well... that is a very clear and sensible technical explanation. Re-calibrating the laser power from the exchange first is a logical first step before digging up wires since we depend heavily on this service for remote working and family communications every day.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am submitting the remote laser transmit power boost command to the exchange OLT line card right now across all your connected household devices including laptops, mobile phones, and streaming hardware.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What adjustment does that apply to the optical link because having a reliable home broadband connection is absolutely essential for our daily household work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It increases optical launch power across the passive optical splitter by two point two decibels.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me watch the ONT diagnostic status page while the command executes...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The OLT re-calibration will commit in approximately fifteen seconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The page refreshed! The optical receive power just improved to minus twenty-four point six dBm! And the amber alarm light on the ONT turned solid green!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Minus twenty-four point six dBm sits perfectly in the optimal middle of our GPON optical power operational budget.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is an immediate four-decibel margin improvement! Let me run a continuous packet ping test to my database server...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously passive optical splitters experience minor insertion loss variations as temperature fluctuates across exchange fiber distribution hubs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I have sent five hundred consecutive packets across the gigabit link: zero drops, zero jitter, and round-trip time is down to seven milliseconds!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms the frame boundary errors were caused by marginal optical threshold detection at minus twenty-eight dBm.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Now that we are at minus twenty-four point six, the receiver has ample headroom.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We also recommend ensuring the white SC-APC optical patch cord between the wall box and ONT is free of sharp bends.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I checked the optical cable: it has a smooth, wide bend radius in a protective plastic conduit.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That ensures zero micro-bending losses on the customer premises side.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The connection has been completely stable through a five-gigabyte test replication.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have locked the re-calibrated laser profile on ticket reference OPT-44019-J.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: OPT-44019-J, noted down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our automated optical monitoring platform will poll your ONT telemetry every fifteen minutes overnight.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will alert your engineering team if the light levels ever drift back towards minus twenty-eight.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If optical attenuation exceeds minus twenty-six dBm, an automated engineering dispatch will trigger automatically.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is an excellent proactive safety net for our business connection.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we conclude our call, that account contact telephone number was 0117 928 4401, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 0117 928 4401 is my primary contact number.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We have calibrated the OLT laser to minus twenty-four point six dBm, cleared the alarm, verified zero frame drops, and scheduled overnight optical telemetry.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Everything is working with complete perfection. Thank you Alex.
